2024_06_fy25_complete_proposed_budget_ex.paragraph: Oakland Schools' proposed original budget for fiscal year 2024-25, dated April 2024, combining an enterprise-wide executive summary and budget assumptions with fund-by-fund budgets, five-year forecasts and the district's 5-Year Capital Outlay Plan. Proposed total funding for the intermediate school district is $470.0 million against $480.9 million of proposed expenditures, with property tax revenue budgeted to rise 5.8% ($13,675,300) to $249,457,500. The single largest line is the Special Education Fund's PA-18 base distribution to local districts, budgeted at $173,556,600 for FY2024-25, an increase of roughly $14.2 million or 8.9% over the FY2023-24 Amendment 2 budget.
2024_06_fy25_complete_proposed_budget_ex.page:
**What this is**

Oakland Schools (one of 56 Michigan intermediate school districts established in 1962; 2111 Pontiac Lake Road, Waterford, MI 48328-2736) proposed original budget for fiscal year 2024-25, pages footered 04.02.2024. It contains the Enterprise-Wide Executive Summary & Budget Assumptions, budgets and five-year forecasts for the General Education, Special Education and Career Focused Education Funds, budgets for the special revenue, debt service, capital projects, enterprise and internal service funds, and the 5-Year Capital Outlay Plan given first reading April 2, 2024. State law requires an ISD board to submit its proposed budget to each constituent district board for review and comment by May 1 and to adopt by June 30; the item carries a May 21, 2024 board meeting date.

**Enterprise-wide totals (net of eliminated Risk Related Activity Fund amounts)**

| Funding - $470.0M total | Amount | Expenditures - $480.9M total | Amount |
|---|---|---|---|
| Property taxes | $249.5M | Salary, wage and benefits | $86.2M |
| Other local & investment revenue | $44.5M | Purchased services, supplies, dues/fees | $23.0M |
| State source revenue | $23.2M | Electric & natural gas utilities | $1.3M |
| Other financing sources & indirect | $20.7M | Capital outlay | $21.0M |
| Estimated grant award funding | $132.1M | Transfers to LEAs and other funds | $213.9M |
| | | Grant related expenditures | $132.1M |
| | | Payment on existing debt | $3.4M |

**Property taxes and PA-18**

Property tax revenue is budgeted up 5.8% ($13,675,300) to $249,457,500 - GEF $14,009,300 to $14,821,800, SEF $178,188,400 to $188,523,300, CFEF $43,584,500 to $46,112,400. The tax base is 70% principal residence / 30% non-principal residence; no Headlee rollback occurred in 2023-24 and none is expected for 2024-25. Michigan Tax Tribunal reserve is set at .25% of tax revenues, about $623,700; the district has repaid over $13.0 million in property taxes on MTT judgments over eleven years. The PA-18 base distribution to local districts is budgeted at $173,556,600, up about $14.2 million or 8.9%; the FY2023-24 budget also carried a $10,687,000 supplemental distribution, of which $3.8 million was distributed in December 2023.

**Three major funds (FY2024-25 proposed)**

| Fund | Revenue | Expenditures | Surplus/(Deficit) | Ending fund balance |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| General Education (100) | $26,154,400 | $28,787,900 | $(2,633,500) | $5,673,500 |
| Special Education (200) | $199,001,400 | $198,917,000 | $84,400 | $16,671,100 |
| Career Focused Education (600) | $53,813,200 | $57,949,400 | $(4,136,200) | $3,721,000 |

GEF unassigned balance falls to $4,244,000 (14.7% of expenditures, from 20.1%), an intentional spend-down for the residency programs and capital projects. SEF holds $15,496,100 restricted for future special education center facility renovations plus $1,145,200 restricted at the policy 5% target. CFEF restricted balance drops to $3,693,400 (6.4%) as transfers fund campus renovations.

**Personnel**

Staffing rises from 625.7 to 636.4 FTE (the narrative states a net 10.4 FTE increase; the staffing table totals 10.7): 4.0 FTE HR Residency Program, 4.0 FTE Student Services (2.0 nanotechnology, 2.0 robotics consultants), 1.0 FTE cosmetology instructional technician, 1.0 FTE Assistive Materials Center, 1.0 FTE MiPLACE administrator, 0.7 FTE fine arts consultant, and (1.0) FTE Shared Services. Budgets assume a 2.0% across-the-board increase plus steps; the collective bargaining agreement expires June 30, 2024. The blended MPSERS retirement rate is 31.19%.

**Capital, debt and initiatives**

The 5-Year Capital Outlay Plan totals $101,482,000 for FY24-FY29, with $21,069,500 in 2024-25. Fund 404 (CFE Campus Renovations) budgets $18,199,200 against a $9,000,000 CFEF transfer; Fund 406 (Administration Building) budgets $1,429,800. Combined debt service is $3,388,900 ($1,535,000 principal, $1,853,900 interest). Named initiatives include up to $5 million for Literacy Essentials Oakland, a Numeracy Initiative, OSTC secured entrances and welcome centers (Fall 2024) and corridor refresh (Summer 2025), a nanotechnology/AI/synthetic biology lab at the Southeast campus, robotics competition labs, and $1,302,600 of software subsidies reported under Board Policy 3230.
2024_06_fy25_complete_proposed_budget_ex.verbose:
**Document and authority.** Oakland Schools, the intermediate school district serving Oakland County, issued its proposed original budget for fiscal year 2024-25 in April 2024 (115 pages, footered 04.02.2024). It is one of 56 Michigan ISDs established in 1962, located at 2111 Pontiac Lake Road, Waterford, MI 48328-2736. The package holds the Enterprise-Wide Executive Summary & Budget Assumptions; budgets and five-year forecasts for the General Education Fund (100), Special Education Fund (200) and Career Focused Education Fund (600, shown as Vocational Ed Fund in the amendment reports); budgets for special revenue, debt service, capital projects, enterprise and internal service funds; and the 5-Year Capital Outlay Plan, given first reading April 2, 2024. Cited authority: the General Property Tax Act (PA 206 of 1893, MCL 211.24e), Uniform Budgeting and Accounting Act (PA 2 of 1968), Revised School Code (PA 451 of 1976, MCL 380.624 and 380.684) and Bulletin 1022. The ISD board must submit its proposed budget to each constituent district board for review and comment by May 1 and adopt by June 30; the item carries a May 21, 2024 meeting date. Budget policies are 3050, 3100 (at least three amendments yearly), 3150 and 3170; Policy 3230 requires the subsidy report. Fund balance targets: 7.5%-12.5% of operating expenditures for GEF unassigned and CFEF restricted, 5%-10% net of LEA transfers for SEF.

**Enterprise-wide totals.** Proposed funding is $470.0 million - property taxes $249.5 million, other local and investment revenue $44.5 million, state source revenue $23.2 million, other financing sources and indirect revenue $20.7 million, estimated grant award funding $132.1 million. Proposed expenditures are $480.9 million - salary, wage and benefits $86.2 million; purchased services, supplies and dues/fees $23.0 million; utilities $1.3 million; capital outlay $21.0 million; transfers to LEAs and other funds $213.9 million; grant-related expenditures $132.1 million; debt payments $3.4 million. Both are net of eliminated inter-company Risk Related Activity Fund amounts.

**Revenue assumptions.** Property taxes rise 5.8% ($13,675,300) from $235,782,200 to $249,457,500 - GEF $14,009,300 to $14,821,800, SEF $178,188,400 to $188,523,300, CFEF $43,584,500 to $46,112,400 - a conservative estimate against Oakland County Equalization projections of more than 6.0% growth. The base is 70% principal residence, 30% non-principal residence; no Headlee rollback in 2023-24 or expected for 2024-25. Michigan Tax Tribunal reserves are .25% of tax revenues, about $623,700; over eleven years the district has repaid more than $13.0 million on MTT judgments. Investment revenue falls 22.6% to $5,778,700 (GEF $549,500, SEF $2,382,800, CFEF $663,600, Fund 270 $54,300, ONE Fund $337,500, Medicaid $312,000, HR/Finance $20,000, debt service $303,000, capital projects $1,150,000). Other local revenue rises 5.9% to $38,737,200. State source revenue falls 2.9% to $23,215,600, with Section 81 ISD Operations up 2.0% to $4,572,600 and the one-time Sections 147a(3) and 147f MPSERS categoricals removed. Grant award funding falls 14.8% from $155,088,500 to $132,100,000 (state $80,125,000 to $58,065,800; federal $71,820,000 to $71,582,700; local $3,143,500 to $2,451,500), chiefly the loss of a $20 million State of Michigan statewide energy audit grant. Other financing sources net of indirect rise 60.3% to $19,514,700 on capital projects transfers ($6,400,000 to $12,400,000) and debt service transfers ($4,824,700 to $6,224,700).

**PA-18 and payments to districts.** The PA-18 base distribution is budgeted at $173,556,600, up about $14.2 million or 8.9% from FY2023-24 Amendment 2's $159,316,800 (FY2023 actual $148,277,365). FY2023-24 also carried a $10,687,000 supplemental distribution, of which $3.8 million went out in December 2023; none is budgeted for 2024-25 pending the FY24 audit. Projected base distributions: $178,440,900 (2025-26), $183,732,500, $189,159,100, $194,716,800 and $199,329,300 in 2029-30 (the forecast schedule shows $199,328,300). Another $2,450,000 covers group home and medical student support, incarcerated youth, startup assistance, extraordinary contingency, assistive technology and Section 24 payments. Total other financing uses rise 5.5% to $213,903,800.

**General Education Fund.** Revenue $26,154,400 (property taxes $14.8 million, 57% of the total; other local $3.5 million; state $7.2 million; other financing $0.7 million) against expenditures $28,787,900 (General Administration $3,303,300; Finance and Operations $9,816,200; Instructional Services $10,326,000; Plant and Fixed Charges $5,342,400) gives a planned deficit of $(2,633,500). Ending balance drops from $8,307,000 to $5,673,500 - prepaids $29,500, assigned $3,500,000 to $1,400,000, unassigned $4,777,500 to $4,244,000 (20.1% to 14.7% of expenditures). Key movements: Cabinet Initiatives (006) $115,100 to $1,234,000 for the residency programs; transfers out (095) $638,400 to $3,744,300, including $3.2 million to the Administration Building Capital Projects Fund for roofs and boilers and $105,900 to QSCB defeasement; leased facilities (093) $18,600 to $165,500 as the GEF absorbs Print Production rent; Technology Services Administration $154,700 to $238,300 for a MiPLACE administrator; School Culture and Climate $2,604,600 to $1,690,800. The forecast shows deficits every year - $(1,252,000), $(437,200), $(132,000), $(327,300), $(612,600) - with unassigned balance falling to $4.4 million (15.9%), $4.0 million (14.5%), $3.8 million (13.9%), $3.5 million (12.4%) and $2.9 million (9.9%). GEF grants Fund 105 drops from $87,165,000 to $64,000,000 with a $(192,500) ending deficit.

**Special Education Fund.** Revenue $199,001,400 (property taxes $188.5 million, 95% of the total) against expenditures $198,917,000 leaves an $84,400 surplus: program supervision and direction $2,674,300; program operations $11,955,900; plant and fixed charges $8,280,200; PA-18 $173,556,600; LEA transfers and program subsidies $2,450,000. Ending balance is $16,671,100 - $15,496,100 restricted for future center facility renovations, $1,145,200 restricted at the 5% target, $29,800 non-spendable. The Assistive Materials Center rises 17.29% to $1,139,100 with a new Materials Center Specialist as supported materials have doubled in five years; Special Populations serves about 23,500 students with IEPs. Capital outlay holds flat at $113,400 annually. Grants Fund 205 rises to $66,000,000, including $63,150,000 federal, $55,826,800 to other public schools and $3,070,800 for non-public school pupils.

**Career Focused Education Fund.** Revenue $53,813,200 (property taxes $46.1 million, 86% of the total) against expenditures $57,949,400 gives a $(4,136,200) deficit, cutting restricted balance from $7,829,600 to $3,693,400 (15.4% to 6.4%): campus and other program operations $28,943,300; LEA transfers and direct program subsidies $5,713,000; plant and fixed charges $23,293,100. Nineteen state CTE program codes run from 501 Agriculture to 597 Computer Systems Networking. Campus totals: Northwest $5,639,200, Southeast $6,119,300, Northeast $6,373,400, Southwest $5,956,100, total campus operations $24,088,000; the four technical campuses serve about 2,700 students from all 28 constituent districts. CTE staffing adds 5.0 FTE, including four STEM consultants for nanotechnology (Southeast) and robotics (Southwest), plus a Northeast cosmetology instructional technician. Transfers out rise from $9,423,100 to $13,338,200 - $9,000,000 to Fund 404, $3,300,000 to 2016 debt, $915,100 to QSCB defeasement, $104,000 to Fund 406. Regional programs total $6,119,800 annually: early college/dual enrollment tuition $392,000, regional certifications and competitions $118,500, K-12 career readiness LEA support $3,311,000, STEMi $498,300, transportation reimbursement $1,800,000. One Oakland County Sheriff's Department School Resource Officer serves each campus, partially reimbursed in 2023-24 by a Michigan State Police grant and fully locally funded from 2026-27; annual 2016 bond debt service is $2.5 million through 2036.

**Personnel, benefits and utilities.** Staffing goes from 625.7 to 636.4 FTE as of 3/19/24 (business and operations 76.6 to 80.6; programs and services 414.3 to 422.0; other 134.8 to 133.8); the narrative calls this a net 10.4 FTE increase while the itemized additions total 10.7 - 4.0 HR Residency, 4.0 Student Services (2.0 nanotechnology, 2.0 robotics), 1.0 cosmetology instructional technician, 1.0 Assistive Materials Center, 1.0 MiPLACE administrator, 0.7 fine arts consultant (0.3 to 1.0), and (1.0) Shared Services. A 2.0% across-the-board increase plus steps is budgeted; the collective bargaining agreement expires June 30, 2024; non-union step growth is 1.3%, union about 0.9%. Salaries and wages with FICA rise 9.0% to $53,684,400; MPSERS costs 10.9% to $23,320,900; healthcare 14.4% to $7,139,300; other insurances 3.0% to $2,088,300. Of eight MPSERS rates, the common Basic/MIP with Health Care Premium Subsidy is 31.34% through September 30, 2024 and a projected 31.36% from October 1, 2024, with the UAAL stabilization rate falling from 16.89% to 10.58%; the blended budgeting rate is 31.19%. Health care hard caps after 1/1/24 are $21,007.83 family, $16,109.06 individual plus one, $7,702.85 single, projected at $21,848.14, $16,753.42 and $8,010.96 after 1/1/25 on 4.0% medical CPI growth; employees pay about 13% on average. FICA is 7.65% on wages up to $168,600. Utilities rise 27.7% to $1,298,600; the Constellation Energy Services electric supply agreement expires June 2024 with kWh pricing expected to rise over 51%.

**Other funds.** Shared Services & Tuition Programs Fund 270: revenue $19,282,000, expenditures $19,293,600, ending committed balance $3,764,900 (VLAC tuition $2,970,000, ACE $1,029,000, Graduation Alliance $1,900,000, foreign exchange $180,000, shared services $10,985,900). ONE Fund 271, a fiber network of 29 consortium members: revenue $1,362,500, expenditures $1,843,100 including Literacy Essentials Oakland $904,100 and the Numeracy Initiative $300,000; ending committed balance $11,418,700. Medicaid Fund 273: $14,883,900 in and out, with $14,127,300 transferred to LEAs ($12,597,300 service fees, $892,000 Caring 4 Students, $638,000 outreach fees) and roughly $14.1 million expected to reach LEAs. HR/Finance Consortium Fund 277 (22 districts, MiPEER, PowerSchool BusinessPlus): revenue $1,333,500, expenditures $1,310,100, ending balance $575,200; $4,875,000 was transferred from CPDI between FY2012-13 and FY2015-16. School Activities Fund 290: $180,000 in and out, balance $256,200. Debt Service Fund 311 (2016 refunding of the 2007 CFE campus bonds, through 2036): expenditures $2,465,400 ($1,535,000 principal, $928,900 interest), ending restricted balance $8,701,100. Fund 313 QSCB Defeasement (2010 bonds maturing 2027): $1,422,000 in, $772,500 out, balance $1,150,300. Fund 314 QSCB Construction Reserve: $754,700 federal interest subsidy, $925,000 term bond interest, restricted balance $11,804,000. Capital Projects Fund 404: revenue $9,750,000, expenditures $18,199,200 (Phase I $6,336,300 including $2,335,600 trade contracts and $1,452,500 roofs; Phase II building alterations $7,000,000; facilities $4,238,600; instructional capital and STEMi $624,300), ending balance $8,592,100. Fund 406 Administration Building: revenue $3,800,000, expenditures $1,429,800, balance $13,455,700, allocated 50% GEF / 24% SEF / 26% CFEF. Production Print Enterprise Fund 710: revenue $1,827,200, expenses $1,825,400, net position $(975,300). Risk Related Activity Fund 810: revenue $9,721,900, expenses $9,636,600, net operating profit $85,300, ending net position $2,828,500 including a $1,000,000 cyber liability reserve and $760,000 professional liability reserve; compensated absence accruals total $3,306,100 and GASB 101 takes effect for the year ending June 30, 2025.

**Capital plan and initiatives.** The 5-Year Capital Outlay Plan totals $101,482,000 of needs for FY24-FY29 - $19,517,800, $21,069,500, $23,053,900, $8,235,000, $16,023,900 and $13,581,900. The 2024-25 detail splits to Main Campus $2,407,000, Southwest $4,844,700, Southeast $4,653,700, Northwest $4,538,800, Northeast $3,923,700, PP&G $222,400, Summit $52,200 and instructional/curriculum programs $427,000, with facilities $17,283,900 (painting Phase 2 $7,000,000; security, card access, fire and Phase I secured entrances $4,635,800; roofs $1,962,500; lighting and energy efficiency $1,852,800), I.T. $2,788,600 and curriculum/instruction $787,000. Fund 404 is projected to end 6/30/2029 at $(16,487,600) against $83,687,600 of needs and $43,000,000 of transfers in. Initiatives described include OSTC Phase I secured entrances and welcome centers (Fall 2024) and the Phase II corridor refresh (Summer 2025); up to $5 million for Literacy Essentials Oakland; a Numeracy Initiative addressing declining 3rd-6th grade Mathematics M-STEP results; a nanotechnology, artificial intelligence and synthetic biology lab at the Southeast campus and robotics competition labs, both fully available in 2026-27; the STEMi mobile classroom booked at all 28 districts and public school academies; two-year Business Office (June 2024) and HR residency programs funded by the General Education Fund; and mental health work including PREPaRE training with the National Association of School Psychologists (seven certified trainers), BTAM training with Michigan State Police and Oakland Community Health Network, and the Aspire program with New Oakland Family Services, with support given to Oxford, Oak Park, Holly and Clawson. Policy 3230 subsidies total $1,302,600: Xello $346,000, Illuminate DnA $366,000, Nepris $260,000, Atlas Rubicon $142,500, Discovery Education Streaming $138,100, STAMP $35,000, CDX Automotive $15,000. Tuition holds at 2023-24 rates: VLAC K-8 $6,450 resident / $6,650 non-resident (300 FTE), VLAC 9-12 $6,700 / $6,900 (150 FTE), ACE $4,900 (156 students). Cost allocation is 50/25/25 general, 70/15/15 technology licensing, 24/24/52 FTE-based, 50/24/26 space, 73/25/2 transportation miles and 6/75.5/18.5 property tax millage, allocating $29,088,300 total ($13,172,100 / $6,875,100 / $9,041,100). County context cited: 3.1% unemployment as of January 31, 2024 versus 3.7% nationally, 94% of jobs private sector, and the Oakland80 goal of 80% of adults holding a post-secondary credential by 2030.
